items.title: Why your rye starter smells of nail varnish
items.summary: A sharp, solvent smell usually means a hungry starter. Feed it more often, or at a higher ratio, for a few days.

items.title: Autumn flour prices: what's changing
items.summary: Millers expect strong bread flour to rise slightly after a wet harvest. Stoneground and heritage flours are least affected.

items.title: Five shaping mistakes and how to fix them
items.summary: Too much flour on the bench, not enough tension, and shaping too early are the most common reasons a loaf spreads.

items.title: Reader question: can I retard bulk in the fridge?
items.summary: Yes, for up to about 12 hours, if the dough has risen around a third first. Expect a tangier loaf.

items.title: Agents that check their own work
items.summary: A second, independent reviewer catches more mistakes than asking the same model to look again.

items.title: Home Assistant's autumn release
items.summary: New energy dashboards, faster history graphs and better support for Matter locks.

items.title: Self-hosting on a NUC: a year on
items.summary: Power use, backups and the one mistake that cost a weekend: no test restores.
